report.source_text: The CT scan revealed the presence of a predominantly fat‐containing mass with soft tissue components, measuring approximately 13 × 23 × 15 cm. This mass appeared to originate from the anterior mediastinum and extended into the right hemithorax, without a clearly evident shift of the heart and mediastinum to the left. The lesion did not reach below the diaphragm. The lower lobe of right lung exhibited almost complete collapse (Figure 2).

clinician.trajectory_summary: An 18-year-old male was admitted after a car accident with right chest pain and abnormal chest exam findings. Chest CT revealed a large predominantly fat-containing mass originating from the anterior mediastinum extending into the right hemithorax, causing right lower lobe lung collapse. Histopathological examination of the mass confirmed an encapsulated lesion with mature adipose tissue and non-neoplastic thymic epithelial cells, consistent with thymolipoma. The patient underwent surgery with no postoperative complications and was discharged in excellent condition.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: CT scan showed a 13x23x15 cm predominantly fat-containing anterior mediastinal mass with soft tissue components extending into the right hemithorax causing right lower lobe collapse
Histopathology confirmed the mass as an encapsulated lesion comprising mature adipose tissue and islands of non-neoplastic thymic epithelial cells consistent with thymolipoma
The patient had no postoperative complications and was discharged in excellent condition on day 11 after surgery
